questions.q: Which middleware protects against cross-site request forgery?
Which class implements the PBKDF2 password hasher?
Which class splits a list of objects into pages?
What exception is raised when a template cannot be found?
Which function sends an email to the site admins?
Which cache backend stores cache entries in a database table?
Which helper returns an object or raises a 404 error when it does not exist?
Which middleware sets security headers such as HSTS?
Which class signs values so they cannot be tampered with?
Which response class streams its content instead of building it in memory?

After deploying our Django app behind a new load balancer hostname, every request returns HTTP 400 and the error log is full of lines like "Invalid HTTP_HOST header: " followed by the new hostname. It works fine locally with DEBUG=True. Where does Django decide to reject the host, and why does it only happen in production?

We switched to ManifestStaticFilesStorage and now rendering any template that uses {% static %} for a file we forgot to run collectstatic for crashes with ValueError: "Missing staticfiles manifest entry for" the file path. Before the switch the same page just rendered. What code raises this and is there a way to make it fall back instead of crashing?

In development, submitting our signup form crashes with a RuntimeError that ends with "slash), or set APPEND_SLASH=False in your Django settings." The form's action URL is /accounts/signup without a trailing slash. In production (DEBUG=False) the same submit is redirected to the slash URL and the POST data is lost. Which part of Django produces this error and why can't it just redirect?

We store a 'last_step' value in request.session inside a view. When that view ends up returning a 500 error response (we render a custom error page), the session change is never persisted and the browser does not get an updated session cookie, while the exact same code path with a 200 response saves fine. Why are session modifications dropped only for server-error responses?

We enabled the site-wide cache middleware, but our home page is never stored in the cache: every hit renders the view again. The page sets a cookie (a language preference) and the response carries Vary: Cookie. Other pages without that cookie are cached correctly, and pages that send Cache-Control: private are also never cached. What decides that these responses are skipped?
